channel.title: Macro Monitor: Learning Centre
channel.description: A daily economics explainer and country spotlight, each a 10-minute read.

item.title: The Explainer: Keynesian economics
item.description: Born in the wreckage of the Great Depression, John Maynard Keynes's ideas about spending, saving and unemployment shaped the post-war world, fell from favour, and came roaring back in 2008 and 2020.

item.title: Country Spotlight: Saudi Arabia: an oil kingdom racing to reinvent itself
item.description: The world's most important oil exporter is spending heavily to build an economy that can thrive after oil. The ambition is huge; so are the risks.

item.title: The Explainer: The yield curve and why inversions worry markets
item.description: A simple line linking short-term and long-term interest rates has an uncanny record of warning about recessions. Then came 2022-24, when it sounded the alarm and the US economy kept growing.

item.title: Country Spotlight: Brazil: the farm to the world with a fragile wallet
item.description: Brazil feeds much of the planet and sits on vast reserves of oil and iron ore, yet it has struggled for decades with inflation, high interest rates and deep inequality.

item.title: The Explainer: How central banks set interest rates
item.description: A committee meets, a number changes by a quarter of a percentage point, and the effects ripple through the economy for up to two years. Here is how that works, and why it is so slow.

item.title: Country Spotlight: India: a services giant searching for factory jobs
item.description: The world's most populous country is also its fastest-growing large economy. The question is whether that growth can create enough good jobs for hundreds of millions of young people.

item.title: The Explainer: GDP: what it counts and what it misses
item.description: Gross domestic product is the most quoted number in economics. It is brilliant at what it was built to do, and silent on much of what makes life worth living.

item.title: Country Spotlight: Japan: the economy that lived the future first
item.description: Deflation, a shrinking population and enormous public debt were once seen as Japan's peculiar problems. Increasingly, they look like a preview of what other rich countries face.

item.title: The Explainer: How inflation is measured
item.description: Behind every headline inflation figure sits a basket of hundreds of items, thousands of price checks and a surprising number of judgement calls. Here is how it works.

item.title: Country Spotlight: Germany: the workshop of Europe at a crossroads
item.description: Europe's largest economy built its prosperity on cars, machines and cheap energy. Now all three pillars are being tested at once.
